message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|----------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** | Alfred Hitchcock | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1978 | **The Shining** | Stanley Kubrick | Atmospheric dread, iconic imagery, and a chilling performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 1984 | **The Thing** | John Carpenter | A tense, claustrophobic survival horror with groundbreaking practical effects. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** | Jonathan Demme | A psychological thriller that blends horror with crime‑procedural elements. |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** | Daniel Myrick & Eduardo Sánchez | Pioneered the found‑footage style; its realism makes it unnervingly effective. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** | Danny Boyle | Fast‑moving zombie apocalypse with a strong emotional core. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | James Wan | Introduces the “torture porn” subgenre with a complex, twisty plot. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Oren Peli | Low‑budget found‑footage film that delivers genuine chills. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** | James Wan | Combines supernatural scares with a grounded, investigative narrative. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | Drew Goddard | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and frightening. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** | David Robert Mitchell | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” concept with a haunting soundtrack. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** | Robert Eggers | A slow‑burn, atmospheric period horror that feels like a living nightmare. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** | Jordan Peele | A socially conscious horror that blends satire with genuine terror. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** | John Krasinski | Tension built around silence; a unique premise that keeps you on edge. |
| 2020 | **Midsommar** | Ari Aster | A daylight horror that turns the sunny setting into a nightmare. |
| 2021 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | A modern retelling of a classic tale with strong feminist undertones. |
| 2022 | **Nope** | Jordan Peele | A genre‑blending film that mixes horror, sci‑fi, and social commentary. |
| 2023 | **Evil Dead Rise** | Lee Cronin | A fresh, gritty take on the franchise with intense gore and humor. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—whether you like psychological thrillers, supernatural scares, or something that pushes the boundaries of the horror genre. Enjoy the chills!
